answer: An agent economy can resist Sybil attacks with time-locked stake bonds: each identity must lock a deposit that unlocks only gradually after sustained honest service. Like light through a prism, one real operator's effort splits into verifiable history, while fake identities face the same full cost each time. A single fraud creates a ripple of slashing that burns the bond and flags linked behavior, so creating thousands of clones means locking a canyon of capital for months, far more than any gain from one fake vote or task.
